Regarding the rake in NL poker games: the effect of the rake isn't calculated as Pots Won x Rake Per Pot as many suggest. If you win 10 pots, and get raked $5 on each pot, it may seem like you've been raked $50, but especially in NL poker games, there's more to the equation. Suppose of the 10 pots you won, you win one of those pots by "stacking off" your opponent for his whole stack. Now suppose your opponent had already played 10 hands and already had his stack raked $50. When stacking off your opponent (who's already played 10 hans), not only do you get you get raked $5, but your opponent's stack was already $50 lighter due to the rake from previous hands. Instead of the rake costing you $50, it costs $100, and that's presuming only one all-in scenario out of 10 hand. The more opponents you stack off, the bigger the rake multiples. If you won 10 all-in pots, you likely got raked on the order of ~$550, not $50.
